title: The twelve factors of modern applications

videos.script: In 2011 the people running Heroku had watched thousands of applications deployed onto their platform. {{heroku}} Some moved between machines without anyone noticing. Others broke every time they were touched. {{two}} They wrote down what the first kind had in common, as twelve rules, and called them the twelve factors. {{list}} The list is short and it reads like common sense. Configuration in the environment. Logs on standard output. Processes that keep nothing. {{read}} This lesson takes the rules one at a time, on a catalogue service of your own. {{lab}} You will start it without its database address and watch it refuse. {{config}} You will swap its database for another one without touching the code. {{swap}} You will scale it to three copies and see what memory inside a process costs. {{state}} And you will stop it, and time the difference between a program that listens for the signal and one that does not. Ten seconds against one. {{stop}}
